newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli cites "pinhead" mentality in bridge fall.
newsitem.headline: Israeli cites "pinhead" mentality in bridge fall.

text.p: An Israeli official on Friday cited Israelis' "pinhead mentality" in the collapse of a pedestrian bridge at an international sporting event on Monday in which two Australians were killed.

Moshe Peled, the deputy minister of education and sports who appointed a commission to probe the collapse, said investigators had met with the engineer who designed the bridge and are now questioning the building contractors.

"You don't have to be an engineer to understand that the pinhead mentality has done us in again," Peled told reporters. "This you can see if you stand near the bridge and also if you see the bridge on television."
The expression is used frequently in Israel to describe a person who shuns responsibility and counts on others to ensure a job gets done.
It was cited to explain the security lapse that allowed a right-wing gunman to assassinate Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin in 1995.
Israeli officials said the public commission would submit its findings within a week, before the 51-nation Maccabiah Games popularly known as the Jewish Olympics ended.

Competitors from the 370-member Australian team were walking across the bridge over the Yarkon River on Monday ready to lead a march into the Ramat Gan Stadium near Tel Aviv for the opening of the games when the metal and wood structure collapsed.
Two Australians from Sydney, ten-pin bowler Greg Small, 37, and 50-year-old Yetty Bennet, section manager of the men's bowling team, were killed and 43 delegation members were injured.
In Sydney on Friday the two athletes were buried after services attended by hundreds of people.
